question.text: Which film will win the Étoile d’Or at the 2026 Marrakech International Film Festival?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the film that is awarded the Étoile d’Or for best film at the 2026 Marrakech International Film Festival.
question.fine_print:
**Other outcome** resolves if the award goes to a film not listed in the other options (e.g., Alkebulan, Furies, Cairo Shadows, Waves of Silence, and Eklipse), the award is shared among more than one film, there is no winner before January 1, 2027, or any outcome other than the question resolving as one of the other options. 

Any changes to a film's title such as translations do not affect resolution.

The full title of the option for "A Day in the Life of Jo" is A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra.

research:
I've finished the searches. Here is what I found.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding source is the festival's official awards list ("palmarès") for 2026, published on [marrakech-festival.com](https://marrakech-festival.com/en/jury/). Nothing has been published yet. The festival's jury page I found still lists past jurors only. There is no data file to read.
- 2026-11-02: The festival announced 76 films from 39 countries. 14 first and second features compete for the Étoile d'Or, and the winners will be announced at the closing ceremony on Saturday 2026-11-28. [TelQuel](https://telquel.ma/instant-t/2026/11/02/marrakech-2026-le-fifm-devoile-les-films-de-la-competition-officielle-et-le-reste-de-la-programmation_2016142/), [Hespress](https://en.hespress.com/148412-marrakech-international-film-festival-unveils-official-selection.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. The festival runs 2026-11-20 to 11-28, so none of the competition films has screened there yet.
- 2026-11-18: **Chronicles from the Siege has been withdrawn from competition.** Its rights holder, Algeria's Issaad Film Productions, pulled it even though director Abdallah Al-Khatib objected. The producer cited a visit to Morocco by Israeli military officials on 2026-11-09 and said it will return the 2024 Atlas post-production prize it received from the festival. The festival said it had to respect the rights holder's decision. In practice this rules the film out. [Screen Daily](https://www.screendaily.com/news/abdallah-al-khatibs-chronicles-from-the-siege-pulled-by-producer-from-marrakech-festival-competition/5222530.article), [TelQuel](https://telquel.ma/instant-t/2026/11/18/le-film-chroniques-des-annees-de-siege-retire-de-la-competition-officielle-du-fifm_2018720/), [Yabiladi](https://www.yabiladi.com/articles/details/208046/festival-marrakech-retrait-d-un-film.html)
- The jury is Marion Cotillard (president), Claes Bang, Emma Mackey, Gilles Lellouche, Kaouther Ben Hania, Vicky Krieps, Saïd Hamich Benlarbi, Ramata-Toulaye Sy and Andrew Haigh. [Le360](https://fr.le360.ma/culture/festival-international-du-film-de-marrakech-le-jury-de-la-23e-edition-devoile_JOCDNBDJ6BHBRIJQUXLWIHLEDE/)

## 3. Recent news and what each film has won before (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: **A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra** (Jacqueline Lentzou, Greece) won the Golden Alexander at Thessaloniki. It had already won Best Director in Venice's Orizzonti section in September 2026 and screened at the New York Film Festival. [Greek City Times](https://greekcitytimes.com/2026/11/16/golden-alexander/), [To Vima](https://www.tovima.com/culture/jacqueline-lentzou-wins-orizzonti-best-director-at-venice-for-a-day-in-the-life-of-jo-chapter-phaedra/amp/)
- 2026 (autumn): **Congo Boy** (Rafiki Fariala, Central African Republic) won best film at Pingyao. Its sales company also lists Sarajevo Best Feature and Rome Best Director, and its lead actor won Best Actor in Cannes' Un Certain Regard section in May. [Screen Daily](https://www.screendaily.com/news/final-payment-congo-boy-win-top-awards-at-pingyao-film-festival-2026/5220892.article), [The Party Sales](https://www.thepartysales.com/movie/congo-boy/)
- 2026-09: **House of the Wind** (Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu, Cameroon) is a debut. At Venice it won the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize and, according to Benin Web TV, the Lion of the Future for best debut. [Benin Web TV](https://beninwebtv.bj/en/venice-2026-auguste-bernard-kouemo-yanghu-wins-two-awards/)
- 2026-09: **The World Before** (Yoon Dan-bi, South Korea) premiered in Toronto's Platform section and reportedly got a Special Mention in San Sebastián's New Directors section. [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/entertainment/films/20260722/yoon-dan-bis-the-world-before-to-compete-in-toronto-film-fest), [Cineuropa](https://cineuropa.org/495877)
- 2026-05-23: **Ben'imana** (Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, Rwanda) won Cannes' Caméra d'Or for best first feature and the FIPRESCI critics' prize. [AllAfrica](https://allafrica.com/stories/202605250022.html), [New Times](https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/35993/entertainment/cinema/benimanas-cannes-triumph-signals-new-era-for-rwandan-cinema/amp)
- 2026-05/06: **Marie Madeleine** (Gessica Généus, Haiti) premiered in the Cannes Première section and won the Grand Prix at Cabourg. [Le Nouvelliste](https://www.lenouvelliste.com/en/article/268349/grand-prix-2026-au-festival-de-cabourg-pour-marie-madeleine-de-gessica-geneus)
- 2026-02: **Sad Girlz** (Fernanda Tovar, Mexico, debut) premiered in Berlin's Generation 14plus section, where Cinema Tropical calls it a "double Berlinale winner". It then played Tribeca's international competition. [Cinema Tropical](https://www.cinematropical.com/cinema-tropical/double-berlinale-winner-sad-girlz-to-have-north-american-premiere-at-tribeca-2026)
- **Our Share of Sand** (Shalini Adnani, India) is BFI-funded. I found no premiere or awards for it. [BFI](https://www.bfi.org.uk/bfi-funded-productions/our-share-sand)
- Films not on the answer list, which count as "Other outcome": Alkebulan (Morocco), Waves of Silence and Cairo Shadows (all three world premieres), plus Furies (Lebanon) and Eklipse (Austria).

## 4. Base rates
- 2025: The Étoile d'Or went to Promised Sky (Erige Sehiri, Tunisia), which had premiered at Cannes. The jury, chaired by Bong Joon Ho, gave the jury prize to My Father and Qaddafi. [Cineuropa](https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/486837), [ioncinema](https://www.ioncinema.com/news/film-festivals/2025-marrakech-intl-film-fest-promised-sky-wins-letoile-dor-all-the-winners)
- 2024: From memory, not checked: Happy Holidays (Scandar Copti), a Venice Orizzonti prize-winner.
- Pattern (my own reading): recent winners tend to be Arab, African or Global South films that already had acclaim from Cannes or Venice. I did not find a full historical breakdown. With one of 14 films withdrawn, 13 remain, and 5 of those count as "Other outcome". I found no case of a shared Étoile d'Or in recent years, but I did not verify this.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast for this award. None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied (the international feature Oscar, the Ballon d'Or and others) relates to it.
- I found no critics' polls or predictions about the Marrakech competition.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-20: Opening night. Competition screenings run through the week, and the first reviews from Screen, Variety and Cineuropa could indicate how the films are received.
- 2026-11-28: The closing ceremony and awards announcement. The question resolves around 2026-11-29.
- Risks to watch: more films withdrawn in the political fallout from the Chronicles case, or the jury sharing the prize, which would resolve as "Other outcome".

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 9 days. The festival runs 2026-11-20 to 11-28, and the awards are announced at the closing ceremony on 2026-11-28.

**(b) Status quo:** No winner exists yet, and none of the competition films has screened in Marrakech. Without a frontrunner, the default is the prior over the 13 remaining films, weighted by the acclaim each has already earned.

**(c) Base rates:** Recent Étoile d'Or winners skew toward Arab, African or Global South films that already had acclaim from Cannes or Venice:
- 2025: Promised Sky (Tunisia), a Cannes title, confirmed in the research.
- 2024: Happy Holidays, a Venice Orizzonti prize-winner. The research gives this from memory, unchecked.
- 2023: Mother of All Lies (Morocco). This is from my own memory, not the research. If correct, a home film has won recently.

13 films remain after the withdrawal. A uniform prior is about 7.7% each, with 5 films counting as "Other". A shared prize is rare but possible.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **Chronicles from the Siege** was withdrawn on 2026-11-18, so it is effectively out.
- **Ben'imana** (Rwanda) won the Caméra d'Or and the FIPRESCI prize at Cannes on 2026-05-23. It is African, and the jury includes Ramata-Toulaye Sy and Kaouther Ben Hania.
- **House of the Wind** (Cameroon) won the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize at Venice in September 2026, and possibly the Lion of the Future.
- **Congo Boy** (Central African Republic) won Pingyao best film and Best Actor in Cannes' Un Certain Regard, plus prizes the sales company lists at Sarajevo and Rome.
- **A Day in the Life of Jo** (Greece) won Best Director in Venice Orizzonti and the Golden Alexander at Thessaloniki on 2026-11-16. It is the most decorated film, but it is European, which fits Marrakech's recent pattern less well.
- **Marie Madeleine** (Haiti) won the Cabourg Grand Prix.
- **Other outcome** covers the Moroccan entry Alkebulan, Lebanon's Furies and three world premieres. Together these carry real weight.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** The jury, led by Marion Cotillard, could favour a world premiere it discovers at the festival, such as Cairo Shadows or Alkebulan, as a home-country statement after the political row over the withdrawal. The jury could also split the prize. Either would resolve as "Other outcome".

**Adjustments:** I moved up from the 7.7% uniform prior for the African films with major prizes (Ben'imana, House of the Wind, Congo Boy) and moderately for Jo and Marie Madeleine. I moved down for films with less pedigree, Sad Girlz and especially Our Share of Sand. I kept "Other outcome" at about 25%: it covers 5 films plus the chance of a shared prize, and the home film may get a boost. No prediction market covers this award, so there is no anchor.
